newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Eurobourses, dlr firm ahead of US jobs data.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Eurobourses, dlr firm ahead of US jobs data.

text.p: European stock markets consolidated in positive territory on Thursday and the dollar firmed gently in thin holiday trading, with activity muted ahead of U.S. employment figures due on Friday.
London shares were also held back to some extent by a bounce in the already strong British pound, provoking further worries among exporters.
There was little lead from Wall Street, which moved reluctantly higher and then slipped into negative territory after U.S. data which showed slowing second quarter GDP growth.
On the foreign exchange front, the dollar firmed decisively above 118 yen and 1.83 marks after recovering ground against both currencies during the European morning.
The dollar's recovery to above 118 yen came after fears of renewed trade tension with Japan had pushed it lower overnight.

It also firmed against the mark after an early blip below 1.83 marks, but dealers said the U.S. currency lacked the momentum to move out of its one-yen and one-pfennig range. "The dollar is basically range-trading across the board," said Bobby Jasper, trader at Fuji Bank in London.
Paul Coughlin, chief trader at Amex Bank, commented that the dollar "should be fairly rangebound before the (U.S. jobs) data, with tomorrow's payrolls being the main focus."
Economists expect Friday's non-farm payrolls report to show 193,000 jobs were added to the U.S. economy in July.

The dollar has surged as much as 60 percent against the Japanese currency from a post-World War Two low in April 1995 but has fallen back nearly seven percent from the 57-month high of 127.46 yen it hit on May 1.
It was trading at around 118.45 yen at 1430 GMT, on a par with its level late on Wednesday in Europe. Against the mark it was around 1.8365 from 1.8383 late on Wednesday.
Meanwhile sterling was looking robust in Europe, having rebounded above the three mark level, though it was off early morning peaks.

It turned positive after Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown said in a newspaper interview he did not plan a special autumn budget to brake consumer spending, leaving the impression that inflation would be controlled by further interest rate rises.
Britain's leading FTSE 100 share index was in positive territory, but only just, up 6.8 at at 4,934.1 by 1400 GMT, and was taking little comfort from a batch of earnings reports.
"Approaching 5,000 points psychologically is always going to prove an important level and people will ask questions," said Richard Jeffrey, chief economist at brokerage Charterhouse Tilney.
British Telecommunications, drug giant Glaxo Wellcome, engineers TI Group and energy company Lasmo all traded unchanged to lower after their earnings proved uninspiring.
Sterling's bounce back over three marks kept the spotlight on overseas earners ahead of the Bank of England's rate-setting Monetary Policy Committee meeting on August 6-7.
British Steel's chairman and chief executive, Sir Brian Moffat, warned that Britain could move "rapidly from apparent boom to recession" unless action was taken to reverse the pound's rising value.
"The government and the Bank of England should be encouraged to say they think the pound is ludicrously overvalued," he wrote in Thursday's Financial Times.

In Frankfurt the main DAX index of floor trade ended at a record closing high, though trade was described as quieter than in recent days. Dealers said support came from Wall Street's overnight advance and the stable, if slightly weaker, dollar.

One focus was Daimler-Benz AG, whose shares fell 4.5 percent on profit-taking after the German industrial group reported a doubling of first half operating profits, generally in line with market expectations.
The Paris bourse was among the best performers, putting on about 0.7 percent by mid-afternoon, mainly because of the settlement of July futures and options contracts.

One big mover was car maker PSA Peugeot Citroen, which was ahead more than five percent to 726 francs in mid-afternoon after brokers upgraded the stock following a positive sales announcement on Wednesday.
CURRENCIES AT 1430 GMT
The dollar was at 1.8365 marks and 118.45 yen compared with 1.8383 and 118.40 in late trading on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1430 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 6.8 points 4,934.1.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index closed up 17.21 points in bourse trade at 4,438.93.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 18.69 points at 3,087.99
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed in the afternoon in London at $326.35 compared with Wednesday's London close of 326.65. Silver was firmer at $4.46.
